sources.entry: Scrutiny | Hard drive S.M.A.R.T. monitoring with a web dashboard

summary.one_liner: Scrutiny is a hard drive health dashboard that wraps smartd/smartctl S.M.A.R.T. data collection in a web UI with historical tracking and notifications.
summary.what_it_does: Scrutiny runs a collector that uses smartctl --scan to auto-detect connected drives and records their S.M.A.R.T. metrics on a schedule (daily by default). A web dashboard focuses on critical metrics and keeps S.M.A.R.T attribute history so slow degradation is visible. It merges manufacturer S.M.A.R.T thresholds with real-world failure rates to set customized thresholds. It also tracks drive temperature. Notifications for SMART failures, collector errors, and missed uploads can be sent through many services, including email, webhooks, Slack, Telegram, and ntfy. It ships as a Docker omnibus image, a hub/spoke Docker setup with a separate InfluxDB, or a manual install.
use_cases: monitor hard drive health on a home or head-less server
track S.M.A.R.T attribute trends over time
get alerts when a drive is failing
view all server disks in one web dashboard
run smartd monitoring in Docker across multiple servers
how_to_run: docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 8086:8086 --restart unless-stopped -v `pwd`/scrutiny:/opt/scrutiny/config -v `pwd`/influxdb2:/opt/scrutiny/influxdb -v /run/udev:/run/udev:ro --cap-add SYS_RAWIO --device=/dev/sda --device=/dev/sdb --name scrutiny ghcr.io/analogj/scrutiny:latest-omnibus
notable: Customized thresholds based on real-world failure rates, not only manufacturer S.M.A.R.T. limits
Auto-detects drives via smartctl --scan, including many RAID controllers
Notifications for SMART failures, collector errors, and missed uploads, with per-device overrides
Omnibus, hub/spoke, rootless Podman Quadlet, and manual install options
Builds for linux amd64/arm/arm64, freebsd, macOS, and Windows binaries
caveats: README says it is a Work-in-Progress with rough edges
NVMe drives need the extra SYS_ADMIN capability; RAID disks must be passed through to the container
Windows Docker support is marked WIP; some ARM targets have only binaries or limited Docker support
Hub/spoke mode requires running InfluxDB separately
keywords: see if my disk is failing
get notified when a drive dies
